plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A long-lived herbaceous perennial with large, often fragrant, bowl-shaped to fully double blooms held above deep green, glossy divided foliage. A beloved cut flower and garden staple in temperate climates.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; widely cultivated in North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for more than 50 years in the same spot, and in China they have been cultivated for over 1,000 years as symbols of prosperity and honor.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: A compact, suckering deciduous shrub with richly scented, semi-double flowers in deep shades of pink to crimson with golden stamens. It is one of the ancestors of many old garden roses.
plants.location: Native to southern and central Europe and western Asia; grown in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The apothecary rose, a variety of Rosa gallica, was used in medieval medicine, and its petals retain their fragrance when dried, making them ideal for potpourri.

plants.name: Leucanthemum vulgare
plants.description: A hardy perennial wildflower with classic daisy-like flower heads featuring white ray petals around a yellow center. It thrives in meadows, roadsides, and disturbed ground, forming drifts of white across the landscape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (May to August)
plants.location: Native to Europe and temperate Asia; naturalized in North America, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Oxeye daisy flower heads follow the sun during the day, and in folklore the plant is associated with St. John's Eve around June 24.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. Streets and parks in subtropical regions turn violet when it blooms, and fallen petals carpet the ground below.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; commonly planted in California, Mexico, the Mediterranean, and parts of Africa and Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, jacarandas are so abundant that the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City, and in some places a falling blossom was once said to bring good luck.
